about: How long each Mistheim People lives, as a number the Artificer can use (#1650): how long its living memory lasts, and how many retellings an old story has been through. Derived from canon, never invented: each entry cites the file and field it reads (`source`) and the words in it (`quote`, checked by old-history.test.ts). `years` is the middle of the range canon gives, or canon's own figure. `unbounded` marks a People canon says has no natural end (its eyewitnesses never die out, so its old stories never drift). `default` marks a People canon gives no figure for: it takes the story engine's human baseline (`storytelling/biology.ts` NEUTRAL_BIOLOGY, 75 years), listed here so nobody mistakes it for canon. The Supabase `ancestries.lifespan` column is the master (docs/canon.md); its repo copies are the Races page bodies in `scripts/races-<people>-content.mjs` and, for the two human Peoples, the migration that writes them.

peoples.quote: typically remain active into their 70s; withdrawal from route-running usually precedes death by a decade
peoples.note: No range given: active into their 70s, and dying about a decade after they stop running routes, read as 85. The same text says 'somewhat longer than the Markfolk baseline', written when the Markfolk were human; against the orc Markfolk's 80–120 that no longer holds. For the owner.
Canon says longer than a human's but gives no figure, so the baseline stands in. For the owner.
Human-adjacent, read as the human baseline.
